PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 32 years
Gestation: 16 weeks by ultrasound
Indication: Prenatal screening for common trisomies

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Chromosomes analysed: 13, 18, 21
Sample type: Uncultured amniotic fluid

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labelled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. A minimum of four informative markers per chromosome were analysed. Peak area ratios between 0.8-1.4 are considered consistent with normal diallelic patterns.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern
Informative markers: 4/4
Peak ratios: 0.95-1.12

Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern  
Informative markers: 4/4
Peak ratios: 0.89-1.08

Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern
Informative markers: 5/5
Peak ratios: 0.91-1.15

CONCLUSION
Analysis consistent with normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. No abnormality detected.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidy of chromosomes 13, 18 and 21 only. It will not detect:
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Segmental imbalances
- Abnormalities of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination below detectable levels

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full chromosome analysis by karyotyping or chromosomal microarray to follow as per standard prenatal testing protocol.

Authorised by: [redacted name]
Consultant Clinical Scientist
Date: [redacted date]
